title: Cautiously Learning From the Success of Former Leaders
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note cautions against uncritically applying the lessons of successful former CEOs, coaches, and performers to current situations, arguing that success is heavily shaped by uncontrollable context that rarely repeats. It distinguishes between the strategic choices these figures made, which were fitted to a specific moment and shouldn't be copied wholesale, and their more transferable behaviors and skills, which can be selectively applied. The piece recommends reading such books and podcasts selectively, mining them for durable tactics rather than treating their strategies as blueprints.
points: Organizational success is shaped by largely uncontrollable contextual factors that rarely repeat in the future.
Books and podcasts by successful former leaders are said to often over-extrapolate from a single, non-repeatable case.
A key distinction is drawn between transferable skills/behaviors and non-transferable, context-specific strategy.
Readers are advised to selectively mine such sources for tactics rather than adopt strategies wholesale.
The piece frames 'selective learning' as the productive way to benefit from predecessors' success stories.
quotes: Many uncontrollable factors play an oversized role in the results organizations and leaders enjoy.
Success is not easily repeatable when conditions change, and they are always changing.
The skills former leaders showcase, the behaviors they employ, and many of the actions they engage in are often highly transferrable to the future.
But the strategy these leaders followed and the decisions they made to achieve success are not.
When it comes to learning from former highly successful CEOs, coaches, and performers, selective learning works best.
